A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The main text, equations, Figures 1–4, and Appendices A–F can be matched reliably; v3 adds Appendix G and Figure 5. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete material.

before.justification: v2 reports original finite-dimensional GD, LBFGS, and CVXPY experiments in Figure 1, plus empirical singular-value distributions from LBFGS runs in Figure 2.

after.justification: v3 retains the original optimization experiments and empirical spectral results in Figures 1–2. These qualify independently of the added theoretical curves in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Appendix G adds fixed ±1 second-layer weights, requiring at least d positive and d negative weights. This substantially expands expressivity beyond v2's PSD quadratic forms: the equivalent optimization covers all symmetric matrices with nuclear-norm regularization, and spectral denoising changes from one-sided ReLU shrinkage to soft thresholding.

E1.justification: The Gaussian-input quadratic regression experiments are retained. Figure 5 changes the student's constraint at κ*=0.2 and Δ=0.5; the formal allowance of signed teachers is not accompanied by an identified additional evaluated target distribution, dataset, or task.

E2.justification: The Bayes-optimal reference comparisons and theory-versus-GD/LBFGS/CVXPY comparisons in Figures 1–4 are retained. Figure 5 presents regularization curves for the added model variant without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Figure 5 adds a numerical evaluation of the model without the PSD constraint, using κ*=0.2, Δ=0.5, sample complexity up to 0.8, and regularization values from the vanishing limit through 0.5. Existing finite-size experimental protocols and the test-error definition remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G and Figure 5 add a focused analysis of how removing the positivity constraint affects regularization-dependent learning curves and interpolation behavior. Existing spectral validation, threshold analyses, and low-rank analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 1 still reports standard deviations over 16 target/training-set realizations, and Figure 2 still uses 16 LBFGS runs. Figure 5 adds theoretical curves without introducing or changing a statistical uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Results in Figures 1–4 are unchanged. Figure 5 adds predictions without the PSD constraint, including a diverging test-error peak at α=0.5 as regularization vanishes. This differs from the retained PSD model's finite cusp and represents results for an additional model setting.

T1.justification: Appendix G adds a substantive formal extension beyond PSD matrices. Equations (113)–(123) prove equivalence through positive and negative spectral decomposition and nuclear-norm minimization; Eqs. (125)–(128) supply the modified denoisers and two-sided integral J. The original theorem and derivations remain intact.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and concluding discussion retain the same core claims about ERM asymptotics, nuclear-norm regularization, and recovery thresholds. The signed-weight case is presented as an additional extension in Section 3 and Appendix G.

C2.justification: Appendix G explicitly connects the PSD expressivity restriction to positive second-layer weights and explains how signed weights relax that boundary under the requirement of at least d weights of each sign. The main discussion's other limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices E–F retain the numerical integration and convergence settings, initialization, software, optimizers, and GD learning rate. The same code-access statement moves from the appendix opening to Appendix E; no separate implementation or resource disclosure accompanies the new extension.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 89 works and retain their research positioning. Maillard and Kunisky's ellipsoid-fitting paper changes from reference [73] to [45], correcting the duplicated introductory citation and causing renumbering rather than adding a new work.

P1.justification: v3 appends Appendix G, adds its Section 3 cross-reference, briefly expands the Figure 2 discussion, and relocates the code statement. The existing narrative and section organization are largely preserved, with limited citation corrections and some notation defects in the new appendix.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 5, a logarithmic test-error plot with a regularization legend and caption. Figures 1–4 have identical figure content. Other visual changes consist mainly of limited text and equation reflow across pages.

improvement.justification: Appendix G usefully broadens applicability beyond v2's PSD restriction through a constructive equivalence proof and explicit asymptotic formulas. Figure 5 also illustrates the positivity constraint's role in interpolation behavior. These gains supplement an unchanged main theorem and empirical validation. Minor notation defects, especially the malformed penalty in Eq. (124), reduce polish but do not outweigh the extension's benefit.
